title: Operator Scenario Playbooks and Template Library
author: Sofia Rosen
content:
Summary:

This page consolidates operator-facing scenario playbooks and a reusable template library for incident response, staged degradations, automated remediation scripts, and post-incident retrospectives. The goal is to reduce time-to-recovery, standardize communications, and provide tested script snippets and notification templates for common platform incidents (KV cache evictions, GPU pool degradation, model swap, token surge, and prefix-cache corruption).

Audience:
- Platform operators
- Oncall engineers
- SREs and runtime engineers
- Team leads running gamedays and runbook drills

Owners and upkeep:
- Primary owner: eng-platform (oncall rotation)
- Playbook maintainer: Sofia Rosen (eng-platform)
- Quarterly review: platform-ops guild (next review: 2026-05-01)

How to use this page:
1) Select the scenario matching your alert.
2) Follow the checklist and run included verification commands.
3) Copy the incident channel template into PagerDuty/Slack incident channel.
4) If automation is needed, execute the vetted script in the automation sandbox, not directly in production, unless the runbook states otherwise.

Table of contents (quick links):
- KV prefix cache eviction 
- GPU pool thermal/preemption 
- Emergency model swap (fallback to quantized variant)
- Token surge / rate-limiting tailbacks
- Staged degradation (tiered responses)
- Post-incident retrospective template
- Notification and public status templates
- Automation snippets and CLI examples

=== KV prefix cache eviction ===
Intro:
A common cause of sudden latency increases for repeat prompt workloads. This playbook describes fast mitigation, verification, and operator-safe cache rehydration steps. Owner: runtime-kv-team.

Severity and SLO impact:
- Symptom: sudden 3x tail latency on prefix-heavy routes, increased GPU token generation CPU offload.
- SLO risk: P99 latency threshold breaches (SLO: P99 < 500ms for interactive routes).
- Alerting signals: elevated cache miss ratio > 30% sustained for 5 minutes; token cost spike; route-level SLO burn.

Immediate steps (0–10 minutes):
1. Acknowledge alert and create incident channel.
2. Run quick diagnostics: 
   - CLI: rwd-admin telemetry query --service=runtime-kv --metric=cache_miss_ratio --window=5m
   - Check recent config changes: git log --pretty=oneline origin/main -- path=runtime/kv/config
3. If cache miss ratio > 30% and recently-deployed shard topology change is present, trigger controlled rehydration (see step 5).

Safe rehydration procedure:
1. Scale worker pods to +20% to reduce pressure (safe for Dedicated mode): kubectl -n runtime scale deploy/kv-worker --replicas=$(($(kubectl get deploy/kv-worker -n runtime -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}')+2))
2. Run targeted prefix warmup for top 50 prefixes: rwd-tool prefix-warmup --ship=top-50 --parallel=4 --dry-run (inspect outputs)
3. Monitor miss ratio and tail latency every 60s; roll back scaling when stable < 10% miss ratio.

Verification checks (10–30 minutes):
- rwd-admin telemetry tail --route=chat-completion --percentile=99 --window=1m
- Verify error budget consumption decreased and no new 5xx spikes.

Post-incident notes and follow-up tasks:
- Assign owner for KV shard topology review (add to sprint).
- Add synthetic warmup job before future topology rollouts.

=== GPU pool thermal / preemption event ===
Intro:
Thermal events or preemption cause sudden node churn and degraded throughput. This playbook focuses on graceful evacuation, tenant priority preservation, and model fallback triggers. Owner: gpu-fleet-team.

Triggers:
- Node-level thermal alarm or repeated gpunode-restart alerts > 2 in 10 minutes.
- Sudden increase in queued requests and downstream queue backlog > 120s.

Operator steps:
1. Quarantine node: rwd-fleet quarantine-node <node-id> --reason="thermal"
2. Re-route new work away from affected AZ via traffic-weight: rwd-routing set-weight --az us-west-2b --weight=0.1 --duration=15m
3. If tenant critical SLOs at risk, enable emergency model swap by policy: rwd-deploy model-swap --from=llama-2-70b --to=llama-2-70b-q4_1 --policy=graceful --max-concurrency=8

Safety and escalation:
- Do not execute full cluster reboot without approval from on-call lead.
- If eviction rate > 20% across the pool, initiate conference bridge and page the platform lead.

=== Emergency model swap: fallback to quantized variant ===
Intro:
Automatic fallback policies can reduce latency and throughput pressure. This playbook covers manual swaps when automated policies don't trigger.

When to use manually:
- Automated routing failed (observability shows no active fallback)
- There is an ongoing cost or capacity emergency and business accepts minor quality degradation

Procedure:
1. Validate compatibility: rwd-admin model-compat --source-model=redwood/llama-2-70b --target-model=redwood/llama-2-70b-q4_1
2. Run canary (2% traffic) for 10 minutes: rwd-rollout start --model-target=redwood/llama-2-70b-q4_1 --traffic=2% --health-check=latency,p99,error-rate --duration=10m
3. If health checks pass, increase to 25% then 100% with 15m observation windows between stages.
4. If degradation is unacceptable, rollback: rwd-rollout rollback --to=redwood/llama-2-70b --reason="quality-regression"

Canary and validation checks:
- Compare token-quality BLEU-ish/embedding drift on curated prompt set: rwd-eval batch --prompts=canary-1000 --metrics=embedding-drift,perplexity
- Track cost delta: billing diff per-minute for affected tenants

=== Token surge and rate-limiting tailbacks ===
Intro:
Token surges create cascading queuing and burst rate limits. This guide standardizes soft-throttle vs hard-reject thresholds and tenant communication.

Default thresholds (configurable per-tenant):
- Soft throttle: sustained token/sec > tenant.soft_limit for 30s -> reduce concurrency by 25% and add 429 hints.
- Hard reject: sustained token/sec > tenant.hard_limit for 120s -> return 429 with Retry-After header.

Operator interventions:
1. Temporarily raise soft_limit for critical tenants only: rwd-tenant set-quota --tenant=my-critical-tenant --soft=120000 --tmp-ttl=15m
2. Spin up burst-capacity if Dedicated pool has spare capacity: rwd-dedicated burst-capacity --pool=dedicated-us-west-2 --units=2
3. Notify customer success for enterprise tenants if rate-limits applied.

=== Staged degradation (tiered responses) ===
Principles:
- Preserve core interactive cases before batch throughput.
- Apply degradation in predictable stages with clear comms so customers can implement client-side fallbacks.

Stages:
1. Graceful slowdown: add per-req rate-limit hints and increase concurrency timeout to 60s.
2. Model fallback: switch to smaller model variant for non-critical routes.
3. Feature gating: disable non-essential features (e.g., streaming, tool-calls) for lower-tier tenants.
4. Hard shed: return 503 for best-effort routes if platform is saturated.

Operator flow (decision tree):
- If CPU/GPU load > 85% and backlog > 2 minutes -> proceed to Stage 1.
- If P99 > 2x SLO for > 10 minutes -> proceed to Stage 2.
- If error budget > 80% consumed -> Stage 3.
- If all stages fail to restore -> Stage 4 and notify execs.

=== Notification and incident channel templates ===
Incident channel starter (copy into Slack/PagerDuty):
"""
[INCIDENT] Short title: <one-line summary>
Severity: P1 | P2
Start time: <UTC ISO>
Observed impact: <routes/tenants>
Immediate action taken: <summary>
Primary contact: <oncall name> (<pagerduty link>)
Next update: in 10 minutes
"""

Status page public template (succinct):
- Title: Degraded performance for chat-completion in us-west-2
- Status: Investigating / Partial outage / Degraded performance
- Impact: Some customers may see increased latency or 429s
- ETA: monitoring, next update in 30m

Customer communication guidance:
- Always include scope, ETA, and whether mitigation is in progress.
- Avoid technical jargon for CS external comms; provide a technical appendix for enterprise contacts.

=== Automation snippets and CLI examples ===
Warmup job example (bash):
#!/bin/bash
PREFIXES=("user:welcome" "user:search" "user:summary")
for p in "${PREFIXES[@]}"; do
  rwd-tool prefix-warmup --prefix="$p" --concurrency=4 --timeout=30s &
done
wait

Evict and reassign GPU lease (python snippet using rwd-sdk):
from rwd_sdk import FleetClient
fc = FleetClient()
node = fc.find_node_by_label('thermalsuspect')
fc.quarantine(node.id, reason='thermal preempt')

Safe rollback command example:
rwd-rollout rollback --to-version=$PREVIOUS_HASH --wait-for=healthy --notify="ops-team@redwood.ai"

=== Post-incident retrospective template ===
Use this template for every incident with P99 impact or P1/P2 severity. Fill in in Confluence retrospective page and link to this incident.
1. Incident summary (one paragraph)
2. Timeline (mm:ss) — include key commands and screenshots/graphs
3. Root cause hypothesis and evidence
4. Action items (owner, ETA, priority)
5. What went well / what to improve
6. Rollout checklist updates required? (Yes/No)

Action item tracker table (copy into a page):
- Action ID | Owner | Description | ETA | Status
- A-2026-001 | Priya Anand | Add synthetic warmup job to pre-deploy pipeline | 2026-03-01 | in_progress

=== Runbook testing and gameday playbacks ===
Testing cadence:
- Quarterly tabletop for high-risk scenarios (KV eviction, GPU thermal)
- Monthly automation tests validated in canary environment for warmup scripts and model-swap logic

Gameday checklist (operator lead):
1. Prepare sandbox environment and restore synthetic traffic generator snapshot.
2. Run scenario runbook verbatim and time each step.
3. Note gaps, unclear command outputs, and missing owner contact data.
4. Update this library and notify reviewers.

=== Roadmap items and planned improvements ===
Planned near-term (Q1/Q2 2026):
- Integrate runbook verification into CI (synthetic runbook smoke tests)
- Provide a one-click incident channel starter in the Console (templated payloads)
- Build a canary automation job for model fallback policies to run during high-load nights

Medium-term (H2 2026):
- Expand per-tenant graceful degradation policy editor in Console with simulation mode
- Add automated post-incident retrospective generation (timeline + candidate action items)
